## What

A desktop can display the same startup warning for hours because its request-only operator waits for pending migrations before opening HTTP. A live database backup retains AccessShare locks on migration targets for its entire snapshot transaction. The recovery page cannot repair that prerequisite by retrying navigation.

There is a separate transport defect in the old workspace backup hook: it relays every pg_dump byte through the operator's JavaScript event loop to gzip, then relays compressed output through that same loop into a file. Both child processes can therefore wait on the operator even when the compressor is not CPU-bound. WI-6554700010053468 introduced direct Linux descriptor inheritance and direct compressed-file output, retaining the existing other-platform stream path and guard/admission/atomic installation. Its native regression blocks the operator thread, then independently decompresses and compares the complete output, including bytes after the stream boundary.

## Why it matters

A healthy backup progress heartbeat establishes liveness; it does not establish healthy throughput or make an hours-long desktop outage acceptable. Conversely, a migration waiting on a backup is not permission to cancel that backup, weaken admission, exclude source records, or serve new code against an incompatible schema. Keep startup recovery, bulk-transfer repair, and backup completion as separate claims.

## How to apply

1. Establish the actual webview target and its listener. For dev3270 read the owning work item and startup logs. Existing production or staging health does not prove3270 recovered.
2. Inspect the pending migration set and call the existing backup relation proof. Real relation conflicts must remain blocked. A conservative-parser false positive is a different source defect and needs its own distinguishing test.
3. Read backup receipt and producer custody before control operations. Never interrupt a protected progressing producer or restart its host merely to load a new hook.
4. To distinguish gzip work from relay/output backpressure, compare process CPU-tick and IO-byte deltas over the same interval and inspect wait channels. In the Nov19 incident, pg_dump and gzip both waited in sock_alloc_send_pskb, while gzip used36 ticks in5seconds and its Node parent used1131 process ticks. This establishes downstream backpressure, not a complete explanation of all elapsed backup time.
5. The maintained distinguishing test is packages/backup/src/hook-pipeline.integration.test.ts. Original stream relay fails the65537-byte blocked-parent case; native descriptor transfer passes65535/65536/65537 and8MiB+17 full-byte comparisons. Preserve child-failure, guard READY/ACK, stall/progress and atomic-install coverage when editing it. Unknown procfs progress is explicit and must never authorize a stall cancellation; the absolute deadline remains.
6. Temporary owner access may use the existing native dev environment switcher: Ctrl+Alt+2 opens the deployed build; Ctrl+Alt+1 returns to dev. Verify both actualURL and API target in the original owner window. Label this mitigation; it does not establish dev recovery. Respect explicit isolated-runtime pins and vm-release profiles. The incident custodian owns restoring the original target after verified recovery.
